Q: Changing --network-plugin in Azure Kubernetes Service for existing cluster A:

Currently this is possible as per Azure is not longer maintaining Kubenet and will be retire on March 2028

To do so you need to have certain prerequisites as stated in the official documentation

Probably the most important one is that you need to have static allocation

In the most general case if you have Calico you need to first remove the network policy

az aks update --name $CLUSTER_NAME --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --network-policy none

Once this is is done, or you don't have a network policy you can update the network

az aks update --name $CLUSTER_NAME --resource-group $RESOURCE_GROUP --network-plugin azure --network-plugin-mode overlay

Q: Terraform AWS Security Group settings to allow all ports between all VMS A:

For ingress_bacalhau security group rule you have set argument of self = true. This will allow traffic only from another instance which also has the allow_ssh_and_bacalhau security group attached.

In contrast, for SSH with ingress_ssh rule you allow traffic from the whole internet (cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"])

You do not specify clearly from which instance was the nmap scan executed. If this instance does not have the allow_ssh_and_bacalhau security group attached, then the traffic wont be allowed from it.

Q: Need to migrate a production database to a new server in oracle A:

To reduce database downtime, use standby technology.

  1. Install Oracle software only 11g and 12c on the new server.
  2. Perform a hot backup on the old server.
  3. Restore the hot backup to the new server.
  4. Configure the standby between the Oracle servers 11
  5. Make a test migration from 11 to 12 version.
  6. Make a test application on new version DB Oracle 12c
  7. Make a hot backup on the old server.
  8. Restore the hot backup to the new server.
  9. Resync the standby between the Oracle servers 11
  10. Make productive migration from 11 to 12 version.

Q: Which authentication approaches are suited with .NET MAUI Blazor Hybrid and Web App without SSR? A:

JWT is a string, for all means and purposes. You can store it as a string, no differently than any other string setting.

In your example, you can see how http request is sent to the ASP.NET server, the server validates user credentials and generates a token. That token is read on success and stored in the secure storage. And this token is used for authentication in later requests.

The reason secure storage is preferred is because it wont be accessible as plain text ( like in Preferences). (In reality slamming that token inside preferences, especially for android/ios is not that big of a deal. )

Q: EF Core scaffold - unique index with WHERE condition produces a 1:1 mapping instead of 1:n A:

As noted in the linked Github issue for this, there is a workaround by adding a second column to the index. As long as the set of columns in the index key does not fully match the foreign key columns, EF Core will not recognize this as a unique index.

create unique index ux_target_request_active_per_target
on trgt.target_request (target_id, id)
where is_active = true;
